title: Внаслідок удару по житловому будинку у Деснянському районі є загиблий та постраждалі – КМВА
content_c:
Київська міська військова адміністрація повідомила про одного загиблого та 8 постраждалих внаслідок російської балістичної атаки по Києву у вівторок.
(оновлено й додано після 2 абзацу)
"На жаль, внаслідок удару по житловому будинку в Деснянському районі загинула одна людина. Висловлюємо співчуття рідним та близьким. Наразі відомо про чотирьох постраждалих. Усім надається необхідна медична допомога", – йдеться у повідомленні.
"Попередньо, є інформація про 6 постраждалих. З верхніх поверхів будинку відбувається евакуація мешканців. Пожежа в квартирах з першого по восьмий поверхи. Екстрені служби працюють на місці", - написав мер столиці Віталій Кличко.
"Попередньо, восьмеро врятованих людей поранені, рятувальники продовжують евакуацію мешканців з верхніх поверхів" - повідомляє ДСНС.
Джерело: https://t.me/VA_Kyiv/21782

title: Why the lonely in China are hiring 'temporary children'
content_c:

In China's cities, despite the huge crowds, or maybe because of them, residents can feel very isolated.
Now, a new industry being dubbed the "loneliness economy" has emerged, with people hiring themselves out as companions to help the elderly.
The BBC's China correspondent Stephen McDonell visits a company that does just that, to see how their business works.

title: ’How do you explain the deletion of 130 million names?’ Why Indian voters are on the streets
content_c:
Born into a small village in West Bengal, Shahida Fakir had always taken her vote for granted. That was, until it was suddenly taken away. She presented officials with her Indian birth certificate and family land documents from the village going back to 1962.
Both her parents had been on the electoral roll going back decades, so she showed proof of that too. But when the final revised voter list came out in April, Fakir was not on it.
The 38-year-old migrant worker, born into a poor Muslim family, was not alone. Since last year, 130 million names – more than the population of Japan – have been removed from India’s electoral roll through a process known as SIR, or special intensive revision. In the nearly eight decades since India’s independence, never have the voter rolls shrunk by such a huge amount over such a short time.
The Narendra Modi government has called SIR a legitimate exercise to clean up the electoral rolls. Overseen by the election commission, tens of millions of dead and duplicate names have been removed. Yet so have the names of millions of living Indian citizens.
Critics allege that the pledge to “purify” India’s voter roll of illegal immigrants has instead been used for more sinister purposes – disenfranchising tens of millions of Muslims, other minorities, and poor and lower caste communities, who are largely not BJP voters.
In a matter of weeks, nationwide anger at SIR has boiled up and spilled out on to the streets of India’s biggest cities, presenting a formidable challenge to the government. Over the weekend, Delhi was transformed into a high-security fortress of barricades, roadblocks and tens of thousands of police and paramilitaries who detained thousands of people, as they attempted to stop youth-led protests calling for the man who oversaw SIR, the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to step down immediately.
On Monday, opposition parties – who have decried SIR as a “weapon for vote theft” by the Modi government – drew tens of thousands of supporters as they marched through the capital and presented a petition to the supreme court, demanding Kumar’s resignation. The youth-led Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, who were behind the call for Saturday’s action, have vowed to “fight on” in their protests against SIR.
Opposition and civil society leaders allege that SIR has already given the BJP an electoral advantage in states such as Bihar and West Bengal, claims the party denied. Others say the exercise has had even more concerning implications: under changes to SIR unilaterally implemented by Kumar, the election commission has become the arbiter of Indian citizenship, a sweeping overreach of its remit.
The consequences are already playing out in West Bengal, where Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) recently came to power and began a crackdown on “illegal” immigrants, complete with several new detention centres. Civil society groups say Muslims excluded by SIR are being targeted.
Fakir was among them. Just three months after the voter list was published – and while her hearing to challenge her exclusion was pending – she was picked up by police and accused of being an illegal Bangladeshi immigrant.
In July she was pushed over the border to Bangladesh, a country she had never been to nor had any connection with, and remains stuck there. “I have all the documents to prove I am an Indian citizen,” she said in a tearful phone call from the Bangladesh border village where she has been sheltering. “I fell on their feet and begged the police not to send me to Bangladesh but they pushed me over the border.”
A Bangladesh border guard officer confirmed Fakir’s account. “We checked all her documents and are convinced that she is an Indian citizen,” they said. In September, her family submitted a petition to the supreme court challenging her deportation. The Indian government was given a month to respond.
“All I want is to return to my family and my home in India. I am waiting desperately for that day,” she said. The backlog of millions of voters in West Bengal challenging their exclusion means it could be years before Fakir’s case is heard.
Those across West Bengal who have been stripped of their votes speak of their terror of being accused of being an alien in their own land. Some have had benefits taken away. Mohammad Hedayet Ullah Siddiqui, 80, from the North 24 Parganas district, said his grandfather had been a freedom fighter for Indian independence and three generations of his family were on the voter rolls. Yet after SIR, Siddiqui described his “humiliation” on finding his name gone.
“With my name erased from the voter list, I am in constant terror. What if they send me to a detention camp?” he said. “I cannot bear to think about being separated from my children and grandchildren at this age, especially when all my ancestors have been buried in India.”
Critics say the problems began in 2023, when the Modi government changed the process for appointing the three-body election commission, giving majority control to the government for the first time. Within a matter of months, the Modi-led panel had appointed Kumar as the election commissioner in spite of opposition objections.
“For decades, the election commission was one of our more credible, independent bodies, but now that has been eroded,” said Ronojoy Sen, a senior fellow at the South Asian Studies Programme, National University of Singapore.
By the following year, the new election commission body had begun SIR, starting in Bihar, where it immediately raised concerns among human rights groups after more than 6 million names were removed. Not long after the revisions, the BJP won a landslide victory in the Bihar state elections.
Despite concerns over SIR rumbling on for months, it did not spark national protests until the Indian Express newspaper last month revealed that two members of the election commission had raised 14 objections to how voters were being excluded from the rolls, but they were unilaterally overruled by Kumar.
“India has always been a flawed democracy but at least citizens felt they had the right to vote and that elections were regular and fair,” said Sen. “SIR has taken away that right. From how it has been conducted, it’s difficult to see how the motive was anything other than to enhance the election prospects of the BJP.”
Three former election commissioners have openly criticised SIR as a “hostile exercise” that has undermined the sanctity of the country’s electoral rolls by focusing on the exclusion – rather than inclusion – of voters. OP Rawat, a former chief election commissioner, described changes to the voter registration form as “wrong and illegal”.
Ashok Lavasa, who was an election commissioner between 2018 and 2020, called for the SIR to be scrapped. “An unfair procedure has been imposed on millions of people in the country, and you have the judiciary which has validated that,” he said last month. “How do you explain the deletion of 130 million names?”
None have been more vehement in their opposition than SY Qureshi, who was chief election commissioner between 2010 and 2012. “This is a national harassment exercise designed to throw Muslims off the electoral roll,” he claimed. “The only way to restore the credibility of India’s elections is to restore those deleted voters.”
The BJP has denied any political involvement or motive in the SIR process, accusing the opposition Congress party of “jealousy” over its recent electoral victories and saying any deleted voters can simply re-enrol. The BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said the allegations were “disinformation” and part of an opposition campaign “being orchestrated to create an atmosphere of division and anarchy”.
Nonetheless, the election commission has appeared to accept some flaws in the process. Late last week, it belatedly put a cap on the number of voter deletion forms – which allow people to submit objections on behalf of others – after incidents in which people submitted thousands of forms targeting legitimate Muslim voters.
Public anger, meanwhile, has continued to build. In Delhi, where the SIR exercise left millions of people off the draft list, protests are expected to continue this week.
A Delhi resident for 30 years, Prashant Tandon, 60, said he could not believe it when a notice came to his door, questioning his life as a voter. “If someone doubts my citizenship, they should produce evidence against me,” he said furiously, adding that he would be protesting alongside the young people. “I should not have to prove that I am an Indian citizen.”

Within a matter of months, the Modi-led panel had appointed Kumar as the election commissioner in spite of opposition objections.
“For decades, the election commission was one of our more credible, independent bodies, but now that has been eroded,” said Ronojoy Sen, a senior fellow at the South Asian Studies Programme, National University of Singapore.
By the following year, the new election commission body had begun SIR, starting in Bihar, where it immediately raised concerns among human rights groups after more than 6 million names were removed. Not long after the revisions, the BJP won a landslide victory in the Bihar state elections.
Despite concerns over SIR rumbling on for months, it did not spark national protests until the Indian Express newspaper last month revealed that two members of the election commission had raised 14 objections to how voters were being excluded from the rolls, but they were unilaterally overruled by Kumar.
“India has always been a flawed democracy but at least citizens felt they had the right to vote and that elections were regular and fair,” said Sen. “SIR has taken away that right. From how it has been conducted, it’s difficult to see how the motive was anything other than to enhance the election prospects of the BJP.”
Three former election commissioners have openly criticised SIR as a “hostile exercise” that has undermined the sanctity of the country’s electoral rolls by focusing on the exclusion – rather than inclusion – of voters. OP Rawat, a former chief election commissioner, described changes to the voter registration form as “wrong and illegal”.
Ashok Lavasa, who was an election commissioner between 2018 and 2020, called for the SIR to be scrapped. “An unfair procedure has been imposed on millions of people in the country, and you have the judiciary which has validated that,” he said last month. “How do you explain the deletion of 130 million names?”
None have been more vehement in their opposition than SY Qureshi, who was chief election commissioner between 2010 and 2012. “This is a national harassment exercise designed to throw Muslims off the electoral roll,” he claimed. “The only way to restore the credibility of India’s elections is to restore those deleted voters.”
The BJP has denied any political involvement or motive in the SIR process, accusing the opposition Congress party of “jealousy” over its recent electoral victories and saying any deleted voters can simply re-enrol. The BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said the allegations were “disinformation” and part of an opposition campaign “being orchestrated to create an atmosphere of division and anarchy”.
Nonetheless, the election commission has appeared to accept some flaws in the process. Late last week, it belatedly put a cap on the number of voter deletion forms – which allow people to submit objections on behalf of others – after incidents in which people submitted thousands of forms targeting legitimate Muslim voters.
Public anger, meanwhile, has continued to build. In Delhi, where the SIR exercise left millions of people off the draft list, protests are expected to continue this week.
A Delhi resident for 30 years, Prashant Tandon, 60, said he could not believe it when a notice came to his door, questioning his life as a voter. “If someone doubts my citizenship, they should produce evidence against me,” he said furiously, adding that he would be protesting alongside the young people. “I should not have to prove that I am an Indian citizen.”
Additional reporting Aakash Hassan

title: Critics warn of espionage risks as Slovakia restores military-diplomatic representation with Russia
content_c:
Concern as Slovakia restores military contacts with Russia
October 13, 2026
When Robert Fico sat opposite Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin in May, the Slovak prime minister said relations between their countries should extend beyond energy supplies.
He told the Russian president that steps had already been taken to restore military attaches at their respective embassies.
Five months later, the arrangement is now taking shape.
Slovakia has sent two military officers — Brigadier General Slavomir Staviarsky and his deputy, Colonel Ivo Gahir — to Moscow and is preparing to receive a Russian military attache in Bratislava, restoring military-diplomatic representation for the first time since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
What has Slovakia to gain?
The move has prompted criticism from opposition politicians, who question what Slovakia stands to gain.
They warn that Russia could use the arrangement to strengthen its intelligence operations.
"One additional military attache does not fundamentally change that broader picture; the appointment's main significance is the political signal it sends," Martin Poliacik, a former Slovak MP affiliated with the opposition Progressive Slovakia party, told DW.
"NATO allies should be concerned both about the activities of the incoming officer and about the political environment in which he will operate," he went on.
The appointments were reported by Slovak news website Aktuality.sk on October 8. Both officers appear on the Slovak Defense Ministry's published list of military diplomats serving abroad.
According to public broadcaster STVR, Staviarsky has been in Moscow since the beginning of August.
Meanwhile, opposition defense experts quoted by Aktuality.sk named the incoming Russian officer as Maxim Verezan.
Verezan has received Slovak approval, according to the opposition sources cited by the website, but was not yet listed among accredited military attaches.
Aktuality.sk says that the Defense Ministry has not answered its question as to when Verezan is due to arrive in Bratislava.
Fear of espionage and disinformation
The prospect has revived memories of a Russian espionage scandal involving Sergei Solomasov, the Russian embassy's deputy military attache in Bratislava, a few years ago.
Solomasov was filmed recruiting and handing over money to Bohus Garbar, a contributor to the pro-Russian website Hlavne spravy, in 2021.
Solomasov was expelled from Slovakia the following year. Garbar was subsequently convicted of espionage and bribery.
Opposition experts told Aktuality.sk that a Slovak attache in Moscow would be closely watched and obtain little useful information, while the reciprocal Russian posting could facilitate espionage in Slovakia.
They warned that the incoming officer could conduct influence and disinformation operations, questioning what Slovakia would receive in return.
Government defends the move
The Slovak government and its supporters have defended the renewal of contacts as a means of gathering information and maintaining diplomatic representation.
In a statement reported by Slovak public broadcaster STVR, Slovak military intelligence said Staviarsky's role was to assess the security and military-political situation and keep the Defense Ministry informed.
Richard Gluck, a member of Fico's Smer party who chairs parliament's defense and security committee, pointed to the presence of American, British and French military diplomats in Moscow.
"We were losing a great deal of information," Gluck told STVR, arguing that ending Slovakia's military diplomatic presence in Moscow had been a mistake.
'A very serious step'
For retired Lieutenant General Pavel Macko, however, the circumstances in which the previous contacts ended are crucial.
"This is a very serious step taken by the Fico government," said Macko, a former Slovak deputy chief of defense and once the highest-ranking Slovak general in NATO's command structures.
"Nothing has changed [since 2022], just the opposite," he went on.
"Russia's adversarial activities continue to grow in Slovakia and in the region. The Russian war of aggression against Ukraine continues with high intensity, so do the hostile hybrid activities against Slovakia and its neighbors," Macko said.
He pointed to a foiled plot to burn down a Ukrainian-owned drone factory in eastern Slovakia and suspicions that incidents in Munich and Leipzig were linked to Russian operations based in Slovakia.
Macko also warned that political influence over Slovakia's intelligence services and the government's pro-Russian policies could further damage intelligence-sharing and trust among allies, despite the presence of "a significant number of very professional and trustworthy officers."
One eye on next year's election?
Martin Poliacik, meanwhile, said he suspected political motives lay behind the decision to restore the military attache posts, which comes as Prime Minister Fico eyes his chances of re-election next year.
"[Fico's] best chance of building a credible narrative for the next election is to claim that everyone else is dragging us into war and he alone wants peace," Poliacik told DW.
"I believe he will argue that he is best placed to talk to Putin about ending the war, and that this requires an exceptionally close relationship with him," he went on, adding that Fico tried to keep quiet about the major role played by Slovak arms manufacturers in supplying Ukraine with ammunition.
The ammunition is supplied under commercial contracts, rather than as military aid from the Slovak government.
Poliacik, too, distinguished between Slovakia's formal commitments and confidence in its political leadership. In his view, Western partners have become accustomed to Fico's behavior.
"Slovakia is formally fulfilling its NATO commitments," he went on.
"Formal compliance does not, by itself, settle the question of political trust," Poliacik added. "Predictability, however, is not the same as reliability."
Edited by: Aingeal Flanagan

title: Spionage/Russland: Japanischer Journalist wegen Recherchen auf Kurilen festgenommen
content_c:
Wegen Recherchen auf Kurilen-Inseln Russland nimmt japanischen Journalisten wegen angeblicher Spionage fest
Der russische Geheimdienst FSB hat einen japanischen Journalisten der Zeitung »Hokkaido Shimbun« unter dem Vorwurf der Spionage festgenommen. Die Festnahme sei im Gebiet um die Insel Sachalin im Fernen Osten des Landes erfolgt, meldeten russische Staatsmedien unter Berufung auf den Geheimdienst. Der Mann sei nach Moskau gebracht worden, wo ein Gericht zunächst zwei Monate Untersuchungshaft anordnete.
Der Reporter soll den Angaben nach Material über die Teilnahme von Einwohnern der Kurilen-Inseln an dem seit 2022 andauernden russischen Krieg gegen die Ukraine gesammelt haben. Auf der zur Provinz Sachalin gehörenden Inselgruppe leben nur etwas mehr als 20.000 Menschen.
Streit über Inselgruppe belastet Beziehungen
Die Kurilen sind eine fischreiche Inselgruppe im Pazifik, die die Sowjetunion am Ende des Zweiten Weltkriegs von Japan erobert hat. Moskau und Tokio streiten seither darüber, wem die vier südlichsten Kurilen-Inseln gehören, weshalb es bis heute keinen Friedensvertrag gibt. Einige Inseln der Kurilen befinden sich nur wenige Kilometer von der japanischen Insel Hokkaido entfernt und sind für Russland von militärischer Bedeutung.
Im August hatte ein Besuch von Russlands Präsidenten auf der Insel Iturup die Beziehungen der beiden Nachbarstaaten verschlechtert. Tokio protestierte und bezeichnete die sogenannten Nördlichen Territorien als »ureigenes japanisches Territorium«. Moskau nahm bereits mehrfach ausländische Staatsbürger mit Spionagevorwurf fest, um sie später gegen im Ausland einsitzende Russen auszutauschen.

title: Alexander Schweitzer: Vom Wahlverlierer zum Bundesminister
content_c:
Alexander Schweitzer ernannt Vom Wahlverlierer zum Bundesminister
Im März wurde Alexander Schweitzer als Ministerpräsident von Rheinland-Pfalz abgewählt. Jetzt soll er als Bundesarbeitsminister dabei helfen, Deutschland aus der Krise zu führen. Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier überreichte ihm in Berlin die Ernennungsurkunde.
Am Abend des 22. März 2026 war Alexander Schweitzer die Enttäuschung deutlich ins Gesicht geschrieben. Mit 25,9 Prozent hatte seine SPD fast zehn Prozentpunkte im Vergleich zum vorigen Wahlergebnis eingebüßt und die Landtagswahl verloren - erstmals seit 1987 lag die CDU in Rheinland-Pfalz vor der SPD. Im Mai wurde Gordon Schnieder im Landtag zum Ministerpräsidenten gewählt.
Amtsvorgänger Schweitzer wurde Koalitionspartner: Gemeinsam stellten die beiden im April die Sondierungsergebnisse der neuen schwarz-roten Koalition vor. Schweitzer sprach bei dem Termin deutlich länger als Schnieder, seine SPD hat in der Koalition mit der CDU genau so viele Ministerposten wie die Christdemokraten - trotz gut fünf Prozentpunkten weniger im Wahlergebnis. Bei dem Termin in Mainz versicherte Schweitzer: Es komme jetzt auf eine stabile Regierung an. Man wolle keine "Berliner Verhältnisse" in Rheinland-Pfalz.
Gerüchte über Ambitionen in der Bundespolitik
Nach der Wahlniederlage in Mainz ließ Schweitzer sich zum Vorsitzenden der SPD-Landtagsfraktion wählen. Minister in einer CDU-geführten Landesregierung zu werden, hatte er im Wahlkampf ausgeschlossen. Es dauerte nicht lange, da wurden ihm Ambitionen nachgesagt, von Rheinland-Pfalz in die Bundespolitik zu wechseln.
Sohn eines Binnenschiffers
Schweitzer, aufgewachsen als Sohn eines Binnenschiffers, trat mit 16 in die SPD ein und wurde 2013 mit 39 Jahren der bis dahin jüngste Minister in Rheinland-Pfalz: Er übernahm das Ressort für Arbeit, Soziales, Transformation und Digitalisierung. Knapp zwei Jahre später wurde er Vorsitzender der SPD-Fraktion im Mainzer Landtag. 2024 machte die langjährige rheinland-pfälzische Ministerpräsidentin Malu Dreyer ihn zu ihrem Nachfolger, als sie aus gesundheitlichen Gründen aus der Politik ausschied. Doch diesen Posten behielt Schweitzer nicht einmal zwei Jahre - bis zu seiner Abwahl im März.
Chance auf Aufstieg ermöglichen
In der rheinland-pfälzischen Landespolitik war sein Ziel, die Chance auf einen sozialen und wirtschaftlichen Aufstieg für jeden und jede möglich zu machen, sagt Schweitzer. "Wenn jemand sagt, ich komme nicht aus einer privilegierten Situation, aber ich will was erreichen, durch Bildung, durch mein eigenes Engagement, durch Leistung - dann müssen die Menschen diese Chancen finden", betonte er als Ministerpräsident.
Da er als Erster in seiner Familie Abitur gemacht habe, "haben Gerechtigkeitsfragen und Zugang zu Chancen in der Gesellschaft ganz unmittelbar mit mir zu tun".
Kritik an Bundeskanzler Merz
Gute Voraussetzungen für einen Bundesminister für Arbeit und Soziales. Allerdings hatte Schweitzer in der Vergangenheit auch immer wieder gegen die gewettert, mit denen er nun auf Bundesebene zusammenarbeiten muss.
Nach dem AfD-Wahlsieg in Sachsen-Anhalt Anfang September warf er Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) vor, dieser habe viele Menschen im Zuge der Reformdebatten durch "manche ungeschickte, aber nicht unabsichtliche Äußerungen vor den Kopf gestoßen." Und an anderer Stelle kritisierte er in Medien, "dass die Art, wie Friedrich Merz agiert, wie er Themen in die gesellschaftliche Debatte einbringt, dieser Bundesregierung nicht hilft".
Auch in der Koalitionsdebatte um die Rentenreform, wegen der die nun zurückgetretene Arbeitsministerin Bas erheblich unter Druck stand, sieht Schweitzer noch Diskussionsbedarf. Nach dem Wahldesaster in Sachsen-Anhalt forderte der stellvertretende SPD-Bundesvorsitzende Änderungen an dem rentenpolitischen Reformkurs der Bundesregierung. Vorschläge, bei denen Menschen weniger von dem bekämen, was sie sich erarbeitet hätten, "dürfen von der SPD keine Unterstützung bekommen", bekundete er.
So spricht Schweitzer sich für die Beibehaltung der abschlagsfreien Rente nach 45 Beitragsjahren aus - einer der großen Streitpunkte in der Koalition, wenn es um die Rentenreform geht. Es wird jetzt die große Aufgabe für ihn sein, diese Reform in Berlin umzusetzen.

title: Україну накривають нова хвиля заморозків та небезпека: синоптики забили на сполох і показали мапу
content_c:
Україну накривають нова хвиля заморозків та небезпека: синоптики забили на сполох і показали мапу
Синоптики оголосили перший рівень небезпечності в декількох областях через потужні зливи та нічні заморозки на ґрунті.
В Україні 14 жовтня очікуються заморозки на заході, однак тепло із температурою повітря до +22 градусів буде на сході та Криму.
За прогнозом синопткині Наталки Діденко 14 жовтня погода в Україні буде «досить однорідною». Температура повітря упродовж дня коливатиметься від +11 до +15 градусів тепла, значно тепліше буде у Криму та східних областях — там прогнозується від +20 до +22 градусів вище нуля.
«14 жовтня істотних опадів не передбачається, хмарність чергуватиметься із сонячними проясненнями. І лише на Сумщині, Полтавщині, та Харківщині пройде дощ», — зазначає синоптикиня.
Водночас Діденко зазначає, що найближчим часом в Україні найтеплішою залишатиметься погода у східній частині, а найхолоднішою — у західній.
В Українському гідрометцентрі прогнозують, що 14 жовтня в Україні утримуватиметься хмарна погода з проясненнями.
Упродовж ночі помірні дощі пройдуть на Лівобережжі, а також в Одеській, Миколаївській, Кіровоградській і Черкаській областях. Удень сильні опади перемістяться на північний схід. Найбільш інтенсивні зливи, місцями з грозами, очікуються в Сумській, Харківській та Полтавській областях — тут дощитиме практично цілу добу.
На решті території країни переважатиме суха погода. Вітер буде переважно північно-західний зі та дутиме зі швидкістю 7–12 м/с.
Найхолодніше 14 жовтня буде на заході, а також у Житомирській та Вінницькій областях, де вночі стовпчики термометрів опустяться до +1…+6 градусів тепла, а вдень покажуть + 9…+14 градусів. На решті території нічна температура становитиме +5…+10 градусів, а вдень повітря прогріється до +11…+16 градусів тепла.
Найтепліша погода збережеться на сході та південному сході, де уночі температура повітря коливатиметься від +9 до +14 градусів тепла, а вдень повітря прогріється до +17…+22 градусів вище нуля.
Синоптики також попереджають про небезпечні явища у низці регіонів України, де оголошено перший рівень небезпечності, жовтий. А саме, у Сумській, Полтавській та Харківській областях будуть значні дощі, а у західних, Вінницькій та Житомирській областях на поверхні ґрунту очікується заморозки до -3 градусів нижче нуля.
«Погодні умови можуть призвести до ускладнення роботи енергетичних, будівельних, комунальних підприємств», — зазначають метеорологи.
Раніше синоптики розповіли, якою буде погода у великих українських містах 14 жовтня.
Підписуйтесь на наші канали у Telegram та Viber.

title: Сенаторы обеих партий США требуют от Трампа отменить дизельное соглашение с Россией
content_c:
Двенадцать сенаторов Соединенных Штатов направили президенту США Дональду Трампу письмо с требованием отменить дизельное соглашение с Россией. По их оценке, соглашение обеспечивает Кремлю дополнительные ресурсы для войны и наносит ущерб национальной безопасности США. Обращение подписали шесть республиканцев и шесть демократов. Об этом сообщили на странице украинского журналиста Остапа Яриша в Facebook.
Письмо усилило волну критики соглашения со стороны как демократов, так и республиканцев. Ранее Республиканская партия почти единодушно поддерживала внешнеполитические решения Трампа. Теперь это единство ослабевает за несколько недель до промежуточных выборов 3 ноября, которые определят, сохранят ли республиканцы контроль над Конгрессом.
«Соглашение, которое вы заключили с Владимиром Путиным, не будет способствовать достижению справедливых целей и не принесет пользы американцам. Оно лишь дает Путину дополнительные ресурсы для финансирования его военной машины и позволяет России продолжать жестокие атаки на украинских мирных жителей», — подчеркнули подписанты.
Сенаторы также раскритиковали предоставление Москве возможности беспрепятственно продавать дизельное топливо на мировых рынках. Они считают, что это противоречит интересам национальной безопасности США. В письме такой шаг назвали предательством украинского народа, который продолжает защищаться от российской войны.
«Это соглашение — подарок нашему противнику и предательство наших союзников. Его необходимо отменить», — отметили сенаторы.
Законодатели напомнили, что на протяжении десятилетий Соединенные Штаты выступали оплотом свободы в борьбе с тиранией. Американские президенты, по их словам, олицетворяли сопротивление страны тиранам.
«Путин — тиран. Выйдите из этого соглашения и воспользуйтесь полномочиями, предусмотренными законом Линдси Грэма. Сохраните наше наследие и выполняйте долг Америки как лидера свободного мира», — подытожили законодатели.
Среди подписавшихся названы Блументаль — демократ, Тиллис — республиканец, Шагин — демократка, Коллинз — республиканка, Дурбин — демократ и Армстронг — республиканец. Также письмо подписали демократы Уайтхаус, Рид и Кунс, а также республиканцы Мурковски, Макконнелл и Корнин.
В течение выходных по поводу этого соглашения также высказывались другие сенаторы и члены Палаты представителей от обеих партий. Они публиковали обращения, отправляли письма и делали публичные заявления. Коллинз, Мурковски и Тиллис ещё в воскресенье, 11 октября, вместе с демократами обнародовали заявление с призывом к Трампу изменить курс в отношении соглашения. Они утверждали, что соглашение противоречит американскому закону, запрещающему импорт российских энергоносителей до тех пор, пока Москва не прекратит агрессию против Украины.
Ранее во вторник Трампа спросили о дизельном соглашении. Однако президент уклонился от ответа на вопрос, сможет ли Россия использовать полученные доходы для закупки новых бомб.
Напомним, что британское правительство заявило о продолжении поддержки Украины после дизельного соглашения Дональда Трампа с Россией. По словам правительственного спикера, Лондон вместе с партнерами и в дальнейшем будет оказывать Киеву финансовую и военную помощь. Великобритания также продолжит санкционное давление на Москву. Пресс-секретарь назвал действующий режим санкций самым строгим из всех, которые вводило Соединённое Королевство.
Кроме того, Владимир Зеленский заявил, что США должны были бы договариваться об экспорте российского дизельного топлива с Украиной. Президент высказал эту позицию 12 октября на Варшавском форуме по безопасности. По его словам, Украина влияет на движение российских судов, работу портов и нефтеперерабатывающих заводов. Зеленский сравнил предложенные Россией поставки 300–500 тысяч тонн дизельного топлива в месяц с мировым потреблением в 120 миллионов тонн. Он считает, что такие объемы не окажут существенного влияния на мировой рынок.

title: Shock, anger and a crackdown: why a contentious electoral revision has sparked outrage
content_c:
Months of simmering public anger have given rise to a season of discontent in India. In its latest iteration, the demand is for the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the scrapping of a controversial electoral rolls revision that has struck 130 million people off the register. Protests have erupted every day over the past week, prompting a violent crackdown on dissenters in the capital.
Over the weekend, Delhi was effectively under lockdown, transformed into a militarised landscape of barricades, road closures and paramilitary forces marching through the streets. Ahead of a protest led by the Cockroach Janta party on Saturday, authorities deployed a massive dragnet: 245 trains to Delhi were cancelled, 45 metro stations were shut, liquor shops were closed, internet services were cut off in the heart of the city and activists were put under house arrest.
The founders of the Cockroach party were removed from an Air India flight shortly after it landed at Delhi airport on Saturday. Opposition leaders were held for more than eight hours in various police stations. Video footage showed students and activists being manhandled, beaten and dragged off the streets while some journalists were also swept up in the detentions. A supreme court lawyer assisting those detained was carried away by police, his shirt torn in the process. The crackdown extended to Mumbai, where Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, was whisked away by the police to prevent him from participating in a local demonstration. On Monday, the Delhi police denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, instead recommending three alternative locations.
“I have been in public life and have watched politics for four decades now, and I have never witnessed this kind of preparation for a demonstration. It was extraordinary by any stretch of the imagination,” political activist Yogendra Yadav, who was also detained, said of Saturday’s crackdown. Despite what he described as “terror unleashed by the state”, he said, small groups staged flash protests in several areas of Delhi defying the heavy security presence.
The crackdown was preceded by similarly aggressive police action against Congress party’s protests, led by Rahul Gandhi. Dramatic images of police personnel detaining Gandhi and his sister, Priyanka, amid scenes of chaos flashed across screens nationwide.
The ruling Bharatiya Janata party has defended its position, with spokesperson Ravi Shankar Prasad accusing the opposition of weaponising protests after electoral defeats. “One, Indian democracy has thwarted attempts to incite anarchy. Two, the country will be governed by parliament, not by the streets,” he said at a news briefing.
While suppression of protests is not new, what stands out this time is the scale of the crackdown in the capital. Government clampdowns in Indian-administered Kashmir have been far more severe, particularly in 2019, when sweeping restrictions were imposed after the revocation of Article 370.
The ferocity of the state response reflects the high political stakes for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government, which faces mounting resistance over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and questions about the credibility of the electoral process.
The latest protests began with a demand for Kumar’s resignation after an Indian Express investigation reported that the ECI’s two other commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had raised concerns about changes to electoral rolls, registration procedures, and digital systems. While Kumar has not responded to the investigation, the ECI said in a statement that “differing views” were part of the “decision-making process”. But the anger runs deeper. The SIR exercise has faced criticism for putting citizens through a trial by fire and leaving the most marginalised in a Kafkaesque limbo. Critics and opposition leaders have gone further, charging that the exercise was designed to benefit the ruling regime.
Former election commissioner Ashok Lavasa told me that the SIR process is unprecedented and unfair, marking a departure from the Commission’s traditional emphasis on inclusion. “For more than seven decades the ECI took it upon itself, as a duty, to enrol everyone who was eligible to vote. And that was one of the basic differences between how Indian democracy works and how other democracies function, where you need to apply to get enrolled,” he said. Voters accustomed to a “friendly procedure” now face a hostile system, which he said “is not good for democracy” in the long run.
Yadav argued that the SIR controversy has exposed what he describes as a deeper process of democratic capture by the ruling party. “Elections are the only mechanism now left for the regime to stamp its legitimacy and election capture is critical to their survival. And therefore, Gyanesh Kumar is critical,” he said. He pointed to a 2023 law giving election commissioners legal immunity for actions performed in their official capacity, which he said is broader than even the protection afforded to judges.
As to what comes next, he envisions potential for three strands to find common ground: the opposition parties, organised civil society groups, and ordinary citizens. For a government that has shown no sign of budging yet, he said, the calculus will get harder. “The longer they delay, the higher the stakes.”
On Monday, the Keralam assembly passed a resolution seeking Kumar’s removal, as opposition parties marched toward the supreme court demanding action against him. And the Cockroach movement and leftist student groups have vowed to continue protesting. “People have refused to be fearful any longer. They will come again and again,” said left-wing student leader, Danish Ali. “We are living in a democratic country, and protest is a fundamental right that no one can snatch away from us.”
What else we’re reading about
Human rights | South African jurist and former international criminal court judge, Navi Pillay, who is of Indian Tamil heritage, has won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. In a first-person account published in 2023, she wrote about her grandparents, who came from India and worked on a sugarcane farm in South Africa for five years before being allowed to buy land.
Technology | The United States has suspended labour-certification processing for several major technology companies, including top Indian IT firms, as part of a crackdown on what it alleges is a misuse of its flagship green card program, fraud and the displacement of American workers. The impacted companies include Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe. “We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labour certification applications involving these companies,” the US labour secretary Keith Sonderling announced last week.
Climate| Citing a significant rainfall deficit linked to the El Niño weather phenomenon, the Maharashtra government last week announced water cuts of at least 10% across urban areas starting 16 October. The state government had previously declared drought conditions in 74% of the sub-districts.
Guest shelf
A recommendation from someone with great taste
With Delhi in the news for all the wrong reasons, I turned to Mayank Austen Soofi, who writes a daily Delhi column for Hindustan Times, to share a spot he returns to for a moment of reprieve. “Whenever I can, I spend a solitary afternoon at the tiny Sufi shrine of Hazrat Sarmad Shaheed, beside the Jama Masjid mosque. The bazaar outside the shrine is the Walled City’s noisiest quarter, yet inside one can sit in silence beneath the neem tree growing beside Sarmad’s grave. An Armenian Jew from Iran, Sarmad fell in love with a Hindu boy in Sindh, eventually became a naked fakir and settled in Mughal Delhi. Executed by Emperor Aurangzeb, his grave lies beneath a red cloth that recalls his blood-soaked beheading. These days, I linger a little longer at the resting place of a man who would just not submit to power.”
Count it
A number worth knowing
32
At least 32 children from the Indigenous community in Balaghat, Madhya Pradesh, have died since June, the Indian Express reported. An inquiry found evidence of measles and malaria. The children, aged between one and 13, experienced symptoms including high fever, skin rashes and abdominal pain.
Vibe check
For Mumbai-based cinematographer, Arbab Kamal Khan, the fleeting, unguarded moments of everyday life offer the most honest form of documentation. His Instagram account is an extension of this cinematic vision, capturing the languor of slow days, the beauty of the mundane and the quiet air of romance.
“When someone passes away, we don’t remember the curated moments,” he told me. “We always go back to the little things, the moments that are small or intricate.”
For me, the images and videos featuring his parents – their feet across each other besides teacups resting atop an Urdu newspaper, or his dad resting under his wife’s dupatta as she brushes her hair – are particularly striking because older people are rarely afforded such tenderness in visual culture. In his frames, his parents are not only elderly figures but also lovers who continue to find intimacy in each other’s presence.

title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
content_c:
Formula 1: Rwanda to bring Grand Prix back to Africa
October 13, 2026
After nearly 40 years of false starts, motor racing's premier sport is returning to Africa, after Formula 1 announced on Tuesday that Rwanda would soon host a Grand Prix.
The race will be know as the African Grand Prix after a 10-year contract was signed between the parties. With no suitable track ready, Rwanda will build one in Bugesera, southeast of the capital Kigali. F1 said it will be ready "early in the next decade."
The last time F1 raced in Africa was the South African Grand Prix in 1993. While there has since been plenty of talk of the sport returning to the continent, most often mentioning South Africa itself, nothing concrete had happened, until now.
A race in every continent
"Today is a landmark moment for Formula 1," F1 President and chief executive Stefano Domenicali said. "With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the world championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.
"Africa has always been part of Formula 1's future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact."
One of the most vocal proponents of a race in Africa has been seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton. The 41-year-old Black British driver, currently with Ferrari, has said he has been "fighting in the background" for years to have a race in Africa. With the date not yet set in stone for the African Grand Prix, it remains to be seen whether he can prolong his career enough to be on the grid when the lights go out in Rwanda.
Kagame all in on sports, but sportswashing claims loom
For Rwandan President Paul Kagame, the event is "a success and a milestone for the entire continent, especially for the African fans." He added that he hoped it could lead to more F1 events in Africa.
Kagame has been president of Rwanda for 25 years, and essentially ran the country for the six years before that, following the genocide in 1994. He routinely wins over 99% of the vote in elections, and the country is often criticized for its human rights record.
The 68-year-old has bet big on sports. Rwanda has had sponsorship deals with a number of top European football clubs, including Arsenal, Atletico Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich. However, fan and media backlash over the deal caused Bayern to drop the commercial element with the country's tourist arm, Visit Rwanda, last year. Arsenal did not renew its deal. Many critics have labeled the policy as sportswashing.
The country also has deals with top US basketball and American football teams, and hosted cycling's Road World Championships last year.
But Formula 1, one of the world's richest sports, will likely be seen as Kagame and Rwanda's biggest sporting coup to date.
Edited by: Jonathan Harding
description: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

title: Fall »Jane Doe«: Cornell-Universität setzt Verbindungspartys aus
content_c:
Wegen Vergewaltigungsvorwürfen Cornell-Universität setzt Verbindungspartys aus
Als Reaktion auf die Vergewaltigungsvorwürfe an der US-Eliteuniversität Cornell hat die Hochschule unter anderem sämtliche Partys und andere soziale Veranstaltungen von Studentenverbindungen für den Rest des noch bis Mitte 2027 laufenden akademischen Jahres verboten. Das solle dabei helfen zu untersuchen, »wie und ob« diese Einrichtungen an der Universität auf sichere Art und Weise weiter existieren könnten, schrieb Universitätspräsident Michael Kotlikoff in einem offenen Brief.
Zudem solle unter anderem mehr Personal eingestellt werden, um von sexuellen Übergriffen betroffene Menschen besser zu unterstützen – beispielsweise wenn sie Anzeige erstatten wollten.
Im Zentrum des Falls steht der Vorwurf einer ehemaligen Studentin, »Jane Doe«, im Oktober 2024 im Haus einer Verbindung von mehreren Männern vergewaltigt worden zu sein. Die Universität Cornell verbot die Verbindung nach den Vorwürfen, verwies aber nur einige der Beteiligten der Hochschule. Strafrechtliche Konsequenzen gab es zunächst nicht.
Aufsehen erregt der Fall auch wegen der schockierenden Details – etwa der vulgären Nachrichten in der Snapchat-Gruppe der Verbindungsmitglieder. Auch gerieten die lokalen Behörden in die Kritik. Zugleich trifft der Fall auf eine seit Jahren geführte Debatte über sexualisierte Gewalt an US-Hochschulen und die Rolle von Studierendenverbindungen. An US-Universitäten kommt es Umfragen zufolge häufig zu sexueller Gewalt gegen Frauen.
Nach einer neuen Zivilklage und wachsender öffentlicher Kritik wird der Fall inzwischen von New Yorks Generalstaatsanwältin Letitia James untersucht.
Was passierte in der Nacht der mutmaßlichen Gruppenvergewaltigung an der Cornell University? Die Aussagen der Studentin und der beschuldigten Männer widersprechen einander stark, nun ermittelt eine Sonderstaatsanwältin. Der Fall spaltet Amerika. Lesen Sie hier weiter.
description: Der Fall einer mutmaßlichen Gruppenvergewaltigung an der US-Eliteuni Cornell sorgt in den USA weiter für Aufsehen. Jetzt kündigt die Hochschule neue Maßnahmen an.

title: Landesweite Demonstrationen: Frankreichs Schüler lassen nicht locker
content_c:
Landesweite Demonstrationen Frankreichs Schüler lassen nicht locker
Ihre Forderungen sind bekannt: bessere Lernbedingungen. Wieder sind in Frankreich deswegen Schulen blockiert, wieder waren mehr als 160.000 Schüler zum Protest auf der Straße. Die Zugeständnisse der Politik sind ihnen bislang zu gering.
Mehr als 160.000 junge Menschen sind laut Polizeiangaben in Frankreich wieder auf die Straße gegangen, um für bessere Lern- und Studienbedingungen zu demonstrieren. Die Veranstalter sprechen von 480.000 Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmern landesweit. Auf Protestmärschen und Kundgebungen in Paris und anderen Großstädten erhielten sie dabei Unterstützung von Bildungsgewerkschaften.
Landesweit wurden laut Bildungsministerium 214 Gymnasien blockiert. Das Ministerium sprach von einem schrumpfenden Rückhalt für die Proteste. Einem Streikaufruf im Bildungsbereich seien nur wenige Beschäftigte gefolgt. Nach Angaben eines Studierendenverbandes waren allerdings auch 90 Prozent der Universitäten blockiert oder geschlossen. Das Hochschulministerium sprach von 35 Prozent.
Wieder Ausschreitungen
Wie schon bei vorangegangenen Protesten gerieten in einigen Städten Polizeikräfte und Demonstranten aneinander. In Nantes setzte die Polizei zum Ende einer Kundgebung Tränengas ein. In Lyon ging die Polizei gegen eine Gruppe schwarz gekleideter Randalierer am Rande des Demonstrationszuges vor, an dem sich etwa 11.000 Menschen beteiligten.
In Paris erhielten demonstrierende Schüler Beifall von Passanten und Busse hupten den jungen Leuten zu. Dort nahm auch der Präsidentschaftskandidat der linken Partei La France Insoumise (LFI), Jean-Luc Mélenchon, teil. Die französische Regierung wirft seiner Partei vor, die Proteste zu instrumentalisieren.
Das Innenministerium meldete am Mittag 30.000 Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer an Protestaktionen an Schulen und 21.000 Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer an den Demonstrationszügen.
Prominente Unterstützung in Saint-Denis
Im Pariser Vorort Saint-Denis mischte sich die schwedische Umweltaktivistin Greta Thunberg unter die Demonstranten. "Die jungen Menschen werden nicht an den Diskussionen beteiligt. Unsere Zukunft wird uns geraubt. Und wie wir hier gesehen haben, erhalten die Schulen nicht die Investitionen, die sie benötigen, was jungen Menschen einfach signalisiert, dass sie in unserer Gesellschaft keine Priorität haben", sagte Thunberg vor Journalisten. Die jungen Menschen aber würden nicht aufgeben und für ihre Zukunft kämpfen.
Sie sei unglaublich stolz auf die französischen Schüler, sagte Greta Thunberg bei dem Protestzug in Saint-Denis.
Die Forderungen, die die Schüler seit Wochen auf die Straße treibt: eine bessere Ausstattung der Schulen, mehr Lehrkräfte und bessere Lernbedingungen. Konkret geht es um fehlende Vertretungslehrer, renovierungsbedürftige Schulen mit kaputten Fenstern und herabfallenden Decken und zu volle Stundenpläne. Besonders in benachteiligten Stadtteilen fühlen sich viele junge Leute als Menschen "zweiter Klasse" und mit ihren Sorgen nicht ernst genommen.
Regierung will Milliarden einsparen
Während in der Nationalversammlung die Beratungen über den kommenden Haushalt anlaufen, wollten in Paris Demonstranten in die Nähe des Sitzes des Premierministers ziehen. Die Demo ist laut Medien nicht genehmigt. Die jungen Leute pochen auf Mehrausgaben von zehn Milliarden Euro für den Bildungsbereich. Bislang sind im Budget für das kommende Jahr 1,2 Milliarden Euro an Mehrausgaben vorgesehen. Außerdem sagte die Regierung kurzfristig den Einsatz von mehr als 3.000 Vertretungslehrern zu, um den ärgsten Unterrichtsausfall zu bekämpfen. Den Protestierenden und den Gewerkschaften reicht das aber nicht.
Die Regierung sieht sich mit den Forderungen nach mehr Geld für die Bildung in einem äußerst ungünstigen Moment konfrontiert. Premier Sébastien Lecornu legte vor einigen Tagen erst einen Sparhaushalt für 2027 vor, in dem Milliardeneinsparungen vorgesehen sind. Denn Frankreichs Staatsverschuldung ist inzwischen auf den höchsten Stand seit 1946 gestiegen und alleine die Zinskosten verschlingen inzwischen Unsummen, die für andere Ausgaben fehlen.
Appell von Präsident Macron
Manche Protestierende zeigen sich bereits entschlossen, nach den Herbstferien im November weiter zu demonstrieren. "Uns ist bewusst, dass die Regierung auf die Ferien hofft, aber wir lassen nicht locker", sagte der 16 Jahre alte Enki Falqui aus Montpellier. Frankreichs Präsident Emmanuel Macron, der sich bislang kaum öffentlich zu den Protesten geäußert hat, hatte am Montag an die Schülerinnen und Schüler appelliert, ihre Anliegen in Ruhe vorzutragen und dabei respektvoll zu sein. Ihre Forderungen seien Themen, "die Zeit und Beratungen erfordern", sagte er.
Oberschüler blockieren seit dem 17. September landesweit den Zugang zu zahlreichen Schulen, um für bessere Lernbedingungen zu demonstrieren. Dabei sorgt nicht nur die Dauer der Protestwelle für Aufmerksamkeit, sondern auch die mitunter gewalttätigen Ausschreitungen. Immer wieder gab es Berichte über angegriffene Einsatzkräfte und Lehrpersonal. 147 Schulbeschäftigte wurden seit Start der Proteste verletzt, teilte das Bildungsministerium mit. Entsetzen herrschte auch, als die Eingangshalle eines Gymnasiums in Nantes brannte und ein Feuerwehrauto in Marseille in Brand gesetzt wurde. Teils wurde auch der öffentliche Nahverkehr wegen der Proteste eingeschränkt.
Schüler sollen Schäden in Millionenhöhe verursacht haben
Die Behörden warfen jungen Menschen Sachbeschädigung und Gewalt vor, die Schäden gehen inzwischen in die Millionen. Das Innenministerium beklagte zwischenzeitlich, die Lage habe nichts mehr mit dem legitimen Äußern von Forderungen zu tun. Vielmehr erfülle sie alle Eigenschaften von städtischer Unruhe.
Umgekehrt wird das Vorgehen der Polizei teils als rabiat kritisiert und es gab den Vorwurf von Polizeigewalt. Tausende junge Leute wurden bei den Protesten festgenommen. Mittlerweile laufen Dutzende interne Verfahren gegen Beamte - etwa, weil ein 15-Jähriger durch eine Blendgranate seine Hand verlor und ein Polizist einem Demonstranten sein Knie ins Gesicht gerammt haben soll.

title: «Має побачити, що від цього залежить його життя»: експерт пояснив, як змусити Путіна до переговорів
content_c:
«Має побачити, що від цього залежить його життя»: експерт пояснив, як змусити Путіна до переговорів
Щоб змусити Кремль шукати вихід із війни, необхідно забезпечити негативну для Росії динаміку на фронті, у кілзоні та в повітрі.
Диктатор Путін продовжує війну проти України, оскільки побоюється, що її завершення змусить його відповідати за скоєне. Водночас він сподівається, що зможе припинити бойові дії, не втративши життя та владу.
Про це в етері Еспресо заявив експерт Національного інституту стратегічних досліджень Олексій Їжак.
За словами експерта, Путін погодиться на переговори тоді, коли усвідомить, що від цього залежить його особисте виживання. Наразі російський диктатор, як вважає Їжак, переконаний, що продовження війни є необхідною умовою збереження його життя та влади.
«Коли Путін піде на переговори? Коли він побачить, що від цього залежить його життя. Зараз його життя залежить від того, що він продовжує війну. Йому здається, що він не може зупинити війну, інакше йому доведеться відповідати за все, що він накоїв», — пояснив Їжак.
Експерт додав, що Путін розраховує на появу обставин, які дозволять йому завершити війну без загрози для власного життя та втрати влади.
Водночас Їжак припустив, що завершення війни може відбутися і за іншого сценарію. У Росії можуть з’явитися люди, готові забезпечити передачу влади та покласти всю відповідальність за наслідки війни особисто на Путіна. У такому разі переговорний процес можуть розпочати вже вони.
«Можливо, з’являться люди в Росії, які готові будуть забезпечити спадкоємність влади при передачі всієї провини за те, що відбулося, особисто на Путіна. Можливо, інші люди підуть на переговори», — зазначив експерт.
На його думку, головне завдання — домогтися припинення війни, незалежно від того, хто саме з російського боку ухвалить відповідне рішення.
Їжак наголосив, що для наближення завершення війни необхідно змінити ситуацію на користь України та створити умови, за яких продовження бойових дій ставатиме дедалі невигіднішим для Росії.
«У будь-якому разі, щоб це наблизити, мають бути баланси. І має бути негативна для Росії динаміка і на фронті, у кілзоні, на землі та в повітрі», — наголосив експерт.
Раніше генерал-лейтенант у відставці Ігор Романенко заявив, що Путін з Трампом хочуть «дотиснути» Україну.
Ми раніше інформували, що диктатор Путін уже отримує політичні переваги від заяв Дональда Трампа про дизельну угоду з Росією.

title: Трамп о разведывательных данных для Киева: США продолжают помогать Украине и стремятся к завершению войны
content_c:
Президент США Дональд Трамп заявил, что США не прекращали обмен разведывательными данными с Украиной. Об этом Трамп сказал во время общения с журналистами, сообщает Fox News.
В частности, президенту задали вопрос, прекратили ли США обмен разведданными с Украиной.
"Нет, не прекращали. Мы им помогали. Но мы действительно помогаем им прийти к окончательному решению. Мы хотим, чтобы война закончилась", — ответил он.
Трамп добавил, что Вашингтон работает с Украиной и с Россией над тем, чтобы положить конец войне.
В то же время журналист спросил, откуда у него уверенность, что глава Кремля Владимир Путин хочет закончить войну больше, чем президент Владимир Зеленский.
“Только благодаря переговорам. Я всю жизнь занимался именно переговорами. Думаю, Путин, наверное, хочет этого. Знаете, честно говоря, они оба хотят, чтобы она закончилась, но не знают, как этого добиться… Мы поможем им этого добиться”, — ответил американский лидер.
Напомним, 9 октября Трамп сообщил, что провел телефонный разговор с главой Кремля Владимиром Путиным и договорился о поставках российского дизельного топлива на американский и мировой рынки.
Через несколько дней президент США заявил, что Украина и Россия согласились на "энергетическое перемирие".
По данным СМИ, представители США угрожали Украине и европейским союзникам прекратить обмен разведывательной информацией и закупки американского оружия для Украины, если Киев не прекратит удары по российским НПЗ.
Также сообщалось, что сотрудники администрации президента США звонили украинскому военному руководству и правительственным чиновникам с требованием не наносить удары по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам после объявления Трампом так называемого энергетического перемирия между Украиной и РФ.
После этого президент Украины Владимир Зеленский заявил, что вечером 12 октября Украина не получила предупреждения от партнеров об угрозе ракетного удара, который нанес удар по Киеву.

По данным СМИ, представители США угрожали Украине и европейским союзникам прекратить обмен разведывательной информацией и закупки американского оружия для Украины, если Киев не прекратит удары по российским НПЗ.
Также сообщалось, что сотрудники администрации президента США звонили украинскому военному руководству и правительственным чиновникам с требованием не наносить удары по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам после объявления Трампом так называемого энергетического перемирия между Украиной и РФ.
После этого президент Украины Владимир Зеленский заявил, что вечером 12 октября Украина не получила предупреждения от партнеров об угрозе ракетного удара, который нанес удар по Киеву.

title: Зеленський: Російський удар балістикою по Києву. Знову без попередження від партнерів. Основна мішень – енергетика
content_c:
У вівторок Росія знову атакувала українську енергетику, партнери не повідомили про загрозу, наразі відомо що РФ планує нові пуски ракет, повідомив президент України Володимир Зеленський.
"Російський удар балістикою по Києву. Знову без попередження від партнерів. Основна мішень – енергетика, а саме ТЕЦ-4. На жаль, є влучання. Також пошкоджений житловий будинок, зараз рятувальники гасять пожежу. Ці ракети були виявлені нашою системою вже фактично на підльоті до Києва. ТЕЦ-4 – один з основних енергооб'єктів Києва… І це точно не справедливо, коли й енергетику вони знищують, і навіть попереджень про запуски балістики Україна не отримує. Важливо, щоб світ про це не мовчав. І важливо, щоб Америка реально бачила, що відбувається і хто винен у тому, що війна продовжується", – написав президент у Телеграм.
За даними української розвідки Росія готує нові пуски балістики. Також Зеленський наголосив на тому, що росіяни не вважають необхідним дотримуватись того, про що раніше заявив Трамп. За словами президента України: "Україна підтримала припинення енергетичного вогню. Росія робить мішенню чергову електростанцію і життя наших людей", – заявив він. Окрім цього Зеленський закликав бути обережними цієї та наступної ночі.
Раніше було заявлено, що оголошене президентом США Дональдом Трампом "енергетичне припинення вогню" між Росією та Україною стосується потенційної угоди про взаємну відмову від ударів по нафтопереробних заводах.

title: 'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
content_c:
'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
Students protests in France have entered their fourth week and with a renewed impetus, according to the BBC's James Waterhouse.
The nationwide demonstrations against poor classroom conditions, including old buildings, teacher shortages and overcrowded classrooms, have caused disruption to education across France as hundreds of lycées (15-18 year-olds colleges) had to be closed.
Students on the streets of Paris told the BBC that they had not achieved anything yet and that stopping now would be a "defeat".

title: Barriers facing black and south Asian music events ‘cost London up to £141m a year’
content_c:
Black and south Asian music events in London face disproportionate cancellations, restrictions and licensing barriers compared with white events, according to a two-year investigation into racial inequality in the capital’s live music industry.
The Race Equality in Music Event Licensing (REMEL) report, led by Black Lives in Music, estimates that cancellations, displacement and events prevented from taking place cost London £127m to £141m annually, with projected losses exceeding £650m over five years.
The report found that genres including Afrobeats, drill and dancehall are routinely labelled “high risk” despite a lack of credible evidence, while indie, pop and rock events face comparatively little scrutiny.
Other events facing stringent restrictions included reggae gatherings aimed at older audiences, jazz nights and community events.
The research raised concerns over the use of unverified police intelligence, with promoters describing events being cancelled based on undisclosed information, online searches or unrelated incidents.
Charisse Beaumont, chief executive of Black Lives in Music, said that although the investigation focused on London, the problems it uncovered exist nationwide.
“As soon as we put the report out there, the call for our survey, people were upset that they couldn’t complete the survey because they were outside of London,” she said.
For Beaumont, the discrimination extended far beyond specific music genres. “It’s about race. And that’s what’s so deeply sad about it.”
The two-year study was commissioned by the mayor’s office and included collaboration by the Greater London Authority (GLA), the Metropolitan Police Service, UK Music, LIVE, the Musicians’ Union and a wide network of promoters, artists, venue operators and community representatives.
The findings suggest that the legacy of the Metropolitan police’s controversial Form 696 persists. Introduced in 2005 as a risk assessment tool, it was scrapped in 2017 after criticism that it discriminated against black music events.
Hakeem Stevens, the report’s lead researcher, said police scrutiny had become harder to document. “Back in the day when emails were sent and faxes were sent, we had documented evidence. Now what’s happening is it’s whispers, it’s phone calls, it’s conversations, verbal conversations that can’t be recorded.”
He said black and Asian performers faced disproportionate scrutiny, adding: “You’ve got white artists that perform black music, and they don’t get given that level of scrutiny.”
Researchers found that promoters received little explanation for cancellations, faced substantial security costs and had limited opportunities to challenge decisions.
Stevens said the financial and reputational consequences could severely affect mental health.
Beaumont highlighted the case of the Colour Factory, a black-owned venue whose licence was suspended after an incident outside its premises that was reportedly unrelated to the venue.
She said the owner successfully challenged the decision but faced significant financial losses, including legal costs and staff redundancies.
“In the end, they won, but they didn’t get their money back,” she said.
The report also found that when incidents occur, many white-owned venues are supported back into business after incidents, while black-owned venues are forced to close for prolonged periods.
Kwame Otiende, a venue owner, promoter and Green councillor, said the additional scrutiny discouraged venues from hosting certain events.
“Venues will have known that they get a lot more grief from whatever relevant authorities they need to go through to get a temporary event notice,” he said.
Instead, he suggested, venues may opt for safer commercial choices: “I could just put your very sort of middle-of-the-road chart music … and I’ll still make the same amount of money.”
The report sets out 19 recommendations, including calls for more transparent, evidence-based licensing decisions, alongside an independent review, clearer evidence standards, better reporting of licensing outcomes and stronger accountability.
Beaumont said: “Success would be for me, the ability for any artist from any background, particularly Black and south Asian, to be able to perform and put on events at any venue without barriers, so they too can make money
“They’ve got an album out, they do a tour, they might be able to do a 1,000-capacity venue, but can they progress from 2,000 to 5,000 to 20,000 to stadium? That doesn’t happen for us.”
The Met police commander Neerav Patel said the force would carefully consider the reports finding. “Our focus will remain on making fair, evidence-based contributions to the licensing process which balance the interests of venues, promoters, artists and local communities while never compromising on our ultimate priority which is to keep Londoners safe” said Patel.

title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
content_c:
Why Germany is backing tougher EU trade defenses against China
October 13, 2026
Germany's cautious approach toward Beijing is cracking. For years, Berlin blocked a harder line on what the European Union describes as China's unfair trade practices.
In the last few months, that caution — a fear of Chinese retaliation that could hurt German exporters — has given way to a willingness to escalate.
Last week, Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron wrote jointly to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen seeking a new tool to cut a trading partner off from the EU's single market if unfair practices continue.
Clearly aimed at Beijing, the letter warned the measure was necessary against countries that "deliberately seek to undermine ... fair market conditions by political or economic means."
China's Commerce Ministry warned Europe would "suffer the consequences" if it adopted such a "kill-switch" plan, which was timed to coincide with crucial EU-China trade talks in Beijing last week.
The cost of standing still
Noah Barkin, a senior adviser with research consultancy Rhodium Group's China practice, told DW that the threats to Germany's export powerhouse "have convinced Merz and his closest advisers that the benefits of action outweigh the costs of inaction."
Before the COVID pandemic, the two economies rose in tandem and German industry benefited from China's ascent.
Since 2021, however, China has fallen from Germany's second-largest export market to its ninth, according to data from Germany Trade & Invest for the first half of 2026.
Chinese competitors have quickly closed the technology gap and benefit from much lower costs and state subsidies. That pressure is being felt especially in Germany's automaking, precision engineering and chemicals industries.
Why Berlin's China policy is changing
German vehicle makers have suffered a large sales drop in China, which was once their second-largest market. According to data from Rhodium Group, German car exports to China plummeted by 66% between 2022 and 2025.
Big German brands now face heavy rivalry from a new wave of Chinese electric vehicle (EV) manufactures in other major markets, including Europe, which is forcing a wave of layoffs and possible factory closures.
In Germany alone, imports of new Chinese-made cars rose 121% in the first seven months of the year, according to Destatis, the federal statistics agency. Overall, Chinese-made vehicles accounted for nearly 14% of total vehicle imports.
"After continuously losing market share in China ... it [the rivalry] seems to be hitting their business within the European automotive market," Andreas Mischer, an associate fellow at the Berlin-based Mercator Institute for China Studies (MERICS), told DW.
Mischer said pressure from Germany's powerful automotive lobby was key to Berlin's "shifting attitude toward trade defense instruments."
Industry pressure grows for trade defenses
Among the many German business leaders who have demanded a more hard-line approach in recent months, Oliver Richtberg, head of foreign trade at VDMA, Germany's mechanical engineering association, was perhaps the most blunt:
"We are currently being deindustrialized through unfair measures — and most companies are no longer willing to accept this," Richtberg told Welt am Sonntag newspaper in August.
According to Eurostat, the wider EU's goods deficit with China was around €360 billion ($402 billion) last year — effectively €1 billion per day — and widened again in the first half of 2026.
While Brussels has been pushing back against the dumping of cheap Chinese goods, a separate industrial protection law and other anti-coercion measures are running into trouble from Beijing and at home.
Business groups question industrial policy proposals
The EU's Industrial Accelerator Act, proposed in March, aims to pull manufacturing investment back to Europe by favoring EU-based firms in public contracts and subsidies.
Foreign investments in key sectors would only be approved if European partners keep majority control, which Beijing has framed as discriminatory.
The European Automobile Manufacturers' Association (ACEA) warned last month that the draft act does little to counter the threat from cheaper Chinese rivals. In a position paper, it said the incentive to produce within the bloc has to be large enough to "cancel out the extra cost of producing locally."
Berlin's chief concern was that China could place new export curbs on rare earth minerals and the magnets made from them. China has a stranglehold on these elements, which are essential for German automotive, renewables and defense manufacturing.
Bloomberg last week cited unnamed German officials as saying that a new EU kill-switch could be a "second-strike weapon" if Beijing blocked those exports. Brussels is also considering unilateral limits on how many hybrid cars China can export to the EU, according to the same Bloomberg report.
EU weighs additional trade measures
Perhaps to avoid such an open confrontation, the EU and China reached a "shared understanding" last week at the EU-China trade talks in Beijing that could cut Chinese exports of hybrid and plug-in hybrid vehicles to the European Union by more than half, according to EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic, who headed the European delegation.
Reports say the agreement would cap such Chinese imports at 350,000 vehicles annually, with the limit increasing by 6% each year over four years.
Overall, new hybrid-electric cars in the EU reached nearly 37% of all new cars registered from January to August, according to ACEA data.
MERICS, meanwhile, calculated that the EU is a more critical export market for China than the US. In the first half of the year, Chinese exports to the EU were $254 billion (€354 billion), versus $172 billion to the US.
This could give EU negotiators a firmer hand as they seek to avoid a trade war while protecting Europe from China's latest export glut.
"The EU has more leverage than it sometimes thinks," MERICS' Mischer told DW.
Edited by: Tim Rooks

title: Zuckersteuer: Koalition legt Streit bei
content_c:
Einigung Koalition legt Streit über Zuckersteuer bei
Die schwarz-rote Koalition hat ihren Streit über die Einführung einer Steuer auf zuckergesüßte Getränke beigelegt. »Die Bundesregierung hat sich auf eine Formulierungshilfe für die Regierungsfraktionen zur Umsetzung der vereinbarten Zuckergetränkesteuer geeinigt«, hieß es am Abend aus dem Bundesfinanzministerium. Die Vorlage soll den Angaben zufolge am Mittwoch im Kabinett beschlossen werden. Zuvor hatte das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND) berichtet.
Der Kompromiss sieht laut RND eine zweistufige Steuer und Ausnahmen für kleinere Hersteller vor. Wie aus der Formulierungshilfe hervorgeht, die auch der Nachrichtenagentur dpa vorliegt, soll ab dem 1. Juli 2027 ein Steuersatz von 26 Cent auf gesüßte Getränke mit einem Zuckergehalt ab 5 Gramm pro 100 Milliliter erhoben werden. Bei einem Zuckergehalt von 8 Gramm pro 100 Milliliter soll der Satz 32 Cent betragen.
Mit der Zuckersteuer will Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) nicht nur Einnahmen für den Bundeshaushalt generieren, sondern auch Getränkeherstellern einen Anreiz geben, den Zuckergehalt zu senken und ihre Produkte gesünder zu machen. Das Kanzleramt hatte seine Pläne jedoch Anfang des Monats vorerst gestoppt. In Regierungskreisen hieß es, sein Entwurf weiche vom Vorschlag der Finanzkommission Gesundheit ab und sei in dieser Form in der Regierung nicht mehrheitsfähig.
Nach der jetzigen Einigung geht die Bundesregierung davon aus, dass die Steuer dem Bund 2027 rund 690 Millionen Euro einbringen wird, im Jahr 2028 dann 925 Millionen Euro. Laut RND soll die Steuer nicht für Hersteller gelten, die weniger als eine Million Liter gezuckerte Getränke pro Jahr produzieren.
Gegen die Steuer gab es bis zuletzt erhebliche Widerstände. Vor wenigen Tagen hatten sich auch die neun Agrar- und Verbraucherschutzminister der Union aus den Bundesländern in einem Brief an Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) dagegen ausgesprochen. Eine Zuckersteuer setze auf staatliche Lenkung und belaste den Kauf bestimmter Lebensmittel unnötigerweise zusätzlich, kritisieren die Ressortchefs in dem Schreiben.

content:
Einigung Koalition legt Streit über Zuckersteuer bei
Die schwarz-rote Koalition hat ihren Streit über die Einführung einer Steuer auf zuckergesüßte Getränke beigelegt. »Die Bundesregierung hat sich auf eine Formulierungshilfe für die Regierungsfraktionen zur Umsetzung der vereinbarten Zuckergetränkesteuer geeinigt«, hieß es am Abend aus dem Bundesfinanzministerium. Die Vorlage soll den Angaben zufolge am Mittwoch im Kabinett beschlossen werden. Zuvor hatte das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND) berichtet.
Der Kompromiss sieht laut RND eine zweistufige Steuer und Ausnahmen für kleinere Hersteller vor. Wie aus der Formulierungshilfe hervorgeht, die auch der Nachrichtenagentur dpa vorliegt, soll ab dem 1. Juli 2027 ein Steuersatz von 26 Cent auf gesüßte Getränke mit einem Zuckergehalt ab 5 Gramm pro 100 Milliliter erhoben werden. Bei einem Zuckergehalt von 8 Gramm pro 100 Milliliter soll der Satz 32 Cent betragen.
Mit der Zuckersteuer will Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) nicht nur Einnahmen für den Bundeshaushalt generieren, sondern auch Getränkeherstellern einen Anreiz geben, den Zuckergehalt zu senken und ihre Produkte gesünder zu machen.
